items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: I took Buster Bailey's place. Buster was playing with Joe before.

ctx.x: Oh. Well, I think I have it straight now. What happened? You went with that one band. Yeah, yeah. Rudy Jackson and Louie.
That's right. Rudy Jackson was in the band. And I took Buster Bailey's place. Buster was playing with Joe before.

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Took Buster Bailey's place for a few months.

ctx.x: Sidney Bechet. We came up together since we were kids in New Orleans. He was playing at the Shea Florence in Marmota. And it was a nice reunion, he and I, for a week or so. And I came back to New York, October 1928. Joined Larry Russell's band in 1929, beginning of the year. And stayed with that band until 1940. 1940. Which was a very pleasant experience and one of the best bands I've worked with. That was the band that we toured with Louis. It was supposed to be Louis Armstrong, but it was Louis Russell…

Like I was in your early days when you were first starting up playing. Yeah. The guys you used to listen to most. Oh. Have perhaps influenced you? Many. The guys from the Kings. Particularly Clare. Well, I tell you. When I was a kid, 14 years old in New Orleans, I used to go up on Sundays to hear Kid Orris Band. He was playing at Miss Coors Lawn. It was a penny party in those days for the kids, you know.
